region: Mardeuil · Vallée de la Marne, Champagne, France
about: Gamet is a family grower estate in Mardeuil, just outside Épernay, born from two families of small growers who began bottling their own Champagne after the First World War: the Garniers of Mardeuil, on the left bank of the Marne, and the Heucqs of Fleury-la-Rivière, on the right. The lines joined when Philippe Gamet and Fabienne Heucq met in 1993. Since 2018 their daughter Marianne, the fourth generation, has run the estate, with her brother Jean-François, an oenologist, helping at harvest and blending. They farm about eight hectares, mostly Meunier.

Rive Droite means “right bank”, and this cuvée comes from the family’s vineyards on the north side of the Marne, in Damery and Fleury-la-Rivière. Old vines, more than fifty years old, grow on sand, clay and limestone studded with shells and fossils, which the family credits for a saline streak. It is a blanc de noirs of Meunier with a little Pinot Noir, fermented with ambient yeasts in stainless steel, put through malolactic fermentation, and aged about twenty months on the lees before a light dosage of around 4 g/l.

In the glass, expect a fresh, fruit-forward blanc de noirs rather than a heavy one. Wine Spectator picked out a clean tang of salinity on the finish, and Vinous called it bright and full of character. The family’s own notes describe Meunier’s soft, round fruit held in check by that seaside-like minerality, and Gault&Millau’s tasters found orchard blossom on the nose with a gentle, refreshing bitterness that lengthens the finish.
facts: Meunier and Pinot Noir (current release 85% Meunier, 15% Pinot Noir)
Damery and Fleury-la-Rivière (right bank of the Marne); vines 50+ years old
Traditional method; ambient yeasts, stainless steel, full malolactic
Brut blanc de noirs, about 4 g/l
